svg.title: Default TCP disk staging versus HIXL and NIXL double-buffered RAM delivery
svg.desc: Comparison of two model loading paths when starting a ModelDeployment: default TCP must finish writing the entire model to target local disk before loading from disk into Device DRAM, whereas HIXL and NIXL alternate between two bounded Host RAM buffers (Buffer A and Buffer B) over multiple cycles to pipeline H2H receive and H2D transfer into Device DRAM.
svg.text: Remote weight delivery vs. default TCP loading
Default TCP finishes writing to disk before loading DRAM; HIXL / NIXL alternates double RAM buffers across multiple cycles into DRAM
DEFAULT (TCP ONLY / REMOTE DELIVERY DISABLED) · DISK FINISHES BEFORE DRAM STARTS
Model stored on source local disk
Target must finish full disk copy first
Starts only after Local Disk is 100%
2. Reads disk into GPU / NPU DRAM
REMOTE WEIGHT DELIVERY (HIXL / NIXL) · DOUBLE-BUFFERED RAM PING-PONG → DRAM
Model already cached on this node
target RAM Buffer A & Buffer B
Fills Buffer A / B in turns
One buffer drains H2D while other receives
Default TCP: 100% Disk first, then DRAM
Multi-cycle RAM H2D fills Device DRAM
